extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors and reviewers in life sciences and medicine considering eLife submission or peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of eLife's Reviewed Preprints peer-review and publishing model: what is reviewed, who decides, outputs produced, fees, and options for Version of Record. Intended to guide authors and reviewers about procedures and expectations at eLife.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint-only review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We only review articles that have been made available as preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife's approach combines the immediacy and openness of a preprint with the scrutiny of peer review by experts; only manuscripts already posted as preprints are eligible for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors are active researchers and select preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors who are active researchers decide which preprints are reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of preprints for review is made by practising researchers serving as editors, implying subject-matter expertise drives review selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative editor–reviewer discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers discuss the reviews with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review process includes dialogue among editors and reviewers to shape assessments, promoting consistency and shared understanding of the manuscript's strengths and weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: No accept/reject decision; publication as Reviewed Preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no accept/reject decision after peer review: rather, every article we review is published on the eLife website as a Reviewed Preprint that includes an eLife assessment, public reviews, and a response from the authors (if available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review produces a Reviewed Preprint record rather than a binary editorial verdict; outputs (assessment, reviews, author response) are made public together with the preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial limits on review/publication volume
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not artificially limit the number of articles we review or publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife's reviewing/publishing throughput is not constrained by quotas, indicating selection is based on criteria rather than slot limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional conversion to Version of Record (VOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: At any point following peer review, authors can choose to have their Reviewed Preprint published as a regular journal article (known as the Version of Record) to mark the end of the publishing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain the option to convert a Reviewed Preprint into a conventional journal Version of Record after peer review completes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee for publishing an article with eLife is $2,000, charged at the point we commit to peer reviewing the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors (or their funders/institutions) are charged a fixed fee when eLife commits to perform peer review, i.e., before completion of the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version of Record complies with funder OA requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of an eLife Version of Record complies with all major funding agency requirements for immediate online access to the published results of their research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife's VOR meets funder mandates for immediate open access; additionally, an increasing number of funders are recognising Reviewed Preprints in research assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife assessment: content and common vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: An eLife assessment that summarises the significance of the findings and the strength of the evidence; the editor and the reviewers write this assessment with the help of a common vocabulary to ensure consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assessment is a concise summary focusing on significance and evidence strength; use of a standard/common vocabulary across editors and reviewers is intended to make assessments consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reviews: strengths, weaknesses, and justification of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Public reviews that describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article, and indicate whether the claims and conclusions are justified by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are public-facing and should explicitly discuss where the work is strong or weak and evaluate whether the data support the authors' claims and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for authors are provided but not published in Reviewed Preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for the authors, including suggestions for revising and improving the article. These recommendations are not included in the Reviewed Preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reviewers/editors give constructive recommendations to authors, those suggestions are not part of the public Reviewed Preprint record (they remain separate from the public assessment and reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional model option (limited period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The model of peer review described above was introduced in January 2023. For a limited period authors can ask for submissions to be reviewed under eLife’s traditional model (which includes an accept/reject decision after peer review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may temporarily opt into the legacy accept/reject model rather than the Reviewed Preprint pathway, but this option is time-limited.
